items.title: Welcome to the ACT Brumbies
items.text:
The Brumbies have been Canberra’s Super Rugby team since the competition began in 1996, drawing players from the ACT and southern New South Wales.

They won Super Rugby in 2001 and 2004, and the Super Rugby AU title in 2020. Club rugby in the region is played for the John I Dent Cup.

The Brumbies have been Canberra’s Super Rugby team since the competition began in 1996, drawing players from the ACT and southern New South Wales.

items.title: From the local club to Super Rugby
items.text:
Every player in the ACT Brumbies squad started at a local club. Talented juniors are picked for representative age-group teams, and the best join the club’s academy.

The academy adds coaching, strength and conditioning, and support with school or work, so players are ready when their chance comes.

data.headline: The ACT Brumbies story
data.standfirst: The Brumbies have been Canberra’s Super Rugby team since the competition began in 1996, drawing players from the ACT and southern New South Wales.

image.alt: Canberra lake with Parliament House in the distance

body.text: They won Super Rugby in 2001 and 2004, and the Super Rugby AU title in 2020. Club rugby in the region is played for the John I Dent Cup.
Home games are at Canberra Stadium, where the club also runs its junior clinics and community days.
1996: The club plays its first Super Rugby season. 2001: Super Rugby champions. 2004: Super Rugby champions again. 2020: Super Rugby AU champions.

data.headline: Match day at Canberra Stadium: what to know
data.standfirst: Tickets, getting there and what to expect at a home game.

image.alt: A stadium under a purple sunset sky

body.text: Home games at Canberra Stadium are a day out for the whole family. Here is how to plan yours.
Members keep the same seat all season. Single tickets go on sale before each game, and children’s tickets are discounted.
Public transport is the easiest way to Canberra Stadium on game day. Allow extra time: the roads around the ground are busy before kick-off.
Gates open well before kick-off, with activities for kids on the concourse. Stay after the game for signing sessions on selected dates.

data.headline: Inside the academy: from club rugby to Super Rugby
data.standfirst: How young players in the ACT and southern New South Wales find their way into the ACT Brumbies squad.

image.alt: A coach with a group of young children on a training pitch

body.text: Every player in the ACT Brumbies squad started at a local club. The academy is the bridge between club rugby and the professional game.
Talented juniors are spotted in club and school rugby and in representative age-group teams, then invited to train with the academy.
Coaching, strength and conditioning, and support with school or work, so players are ready when their chance comes.
The same pathway leads to the club’s Super W team.
